title: How many in total?
keyIdea: The last number you say when counting tells you how many there are.

kid: When you finish counting, the last number you say tells you how many there are.
It does not matter which one you start with. It does not matter how they are laid out. A line of 6 and a messy pile of 6 are both 6.
adult: This is the cardinality principle: the final number word names the size of the whole set. A child who recounts from one when asked 'how many?' can recite numbers but hasn't yet linked the last word to the total.
Two related facts: the order you count in doesn't change the total, and spreading out or bunching up the objects doesn't change it either.

familyTip: Ask 'so how many is that?' after counting. If your child starts again from one, count together and stress the last word.

practice.prompt: You count shells, and the last number you say is {n}. How many shells are there?
practice.hint: Which number did you say last?
practice.explain: The last number you said was {n}, so there are {n} shells.

practice.prompt: 8 counters in a line are pushed together into a pile. How many counters are there now?
practice.hint: Did any counters get added or taken away?
practice.explain: Moving counters doesn't add or remove any, so there are still 8.

practice.hint: Count in a steady rhythm, one triangle per word.

practice.prompt: Lily counts some toys starting with the teddy and gets 6. Jo counts the same toys starting with the car. What should Jo get?
practice.hint: Does the starting point change how many toys there are?
practice.explain: The number of toys is the same whatever order you count them in, so Jo also gets 6.

practice.prompt: {n} counters in a line are pushed together into a pile. How many counters are there now?
practice.hint: Did any counters get added or taken away?
practice.explain: Moving counters doesn't add or take any away, so there are still {n}.

pool.prompt: After counting 'one, two, … nine', someone asks 'How many?' What is the best answer?
pool.hint: The last number you said tells you.
pool.explain: The last number word, nine, is the total.

pool.hint: Count every star across all the groups.

pool.prompt: Ten coins are spread out on a table. Another ten coins are stacked in a tower. Which has more coins?
pool.hint: Count each set in your head.
pool.explain: Both sets have ten coins; the arrangement doesn't change the number.

pool.prompt: You count leaves and the last number you say is {n}. How many leaves are there?
pool.explain: There are {n} leaves: the last number said is the total.

pool.prompt: Stars are in two groups: {a} on the left and {b} on the right. You count every star, one by one. How many stars are there?
pool.hint: Keep counting from the left group straight into the right group.

pool.prompt: A tower of {n} blocks gets knocked over and the blocks scatter across the floor. How many blocks are there now?
pool.explain: Still {n}. Moving the blocks doesn't change how many there are.

pool.prompt: Jay counts 7 cars starting from the red one. Kim counts them again starting from the blue one. What should Kim get?
pool.hint: Does the starting car change how many cars there are?
pool.explain: Kim also gets 7. The order you count in doesn't change the total.

visual.caption: Add red and blue counters. How many altogether? The ten-frame shows how close you are to 10.
